name: Tower Arete

pitch_detail.notes: Rocky ridge ascent (100 feet); scrambling terrain leading to the arete
Low-angled ridge travel (200 feet) along the arete with excellent exposure
Left-side bypass of vertical terrain (175 feet); avoiding the steeper sections of the North Tower Ridge Route
Tower summit approach (90 feet); final approach to top of North Tower
Final crest traverse (75 feet); walking along the ridge to reach Tiffany's main slope

rappels: None documented — descent is a walk-off, not a rappel descent.
descent_text: From the top of the Tower Arete, descend the northwest ridge (mostly 3rd class) to approximately 7,950 feet. Contour northeast and locate the old northeast ridge trail (may be faint). Follow it down to rejoin the main Tiffany Lake trail at Honeymoon Pass. Total descent time 1.5-2 hours.
approach: Drive to Tiffany Springs Campground (elev. ~6,760 ft) via Forest Road 39, accessed either from Conconully (south, via FR-37) or from Winthrop (southwest, via East Chewuch Road and FR-37) — both are long gravel-road drives of an hour or more. From the campground, hike the Tiffany Lake Trail #373 east past Tiffany Lake to Honeymoon Pass (7,150 ft, roughly 45 minutes of easy trail), then leave the trail and traverse south across open grassy slopes to the small cirque at the base of the North Face (about 7,360 ft). The North Face itself rises roughly 650 feet above the cirque, split by couloirs and a rock tower; the whole approach is considered short and easy relative to other Pasayten-area objectives.
overview: A five-pitch alpine ridge route on the north face that follows the same ridge as the North Tower Ridge Route while avoiding its steeper, more technical pitches. Features excellent granite arete climbing with great exposure and views.
beta: A more moderate alpine alternative to the North Tower Ridge Route, following an exciting arete with great exposure but lower technical difficulty. Route can be split into two parts: approach on easier terrain, then a more dramatic arete section. Requires careful attention to loose rock and boulders throughout. Approximately 4-5 hour total time from campground.
